title: Remote rental operations for independent hosts

scope.audience: Provisional: remote independent rental owners and family/local coordinators who struggle with fragmented tools and dependable delegation. Mom, about 66-67, is the concrete initial example in Texas; a broader age-defined segment and initial sales market remain untested.
scope.context: Family rental in Texas, with overseas founders and local family help. Prior incidents and rough frequency estimates retained in scope history and E01-E28. New clarification: walkthroughs continue before almost every arrival and cover cleanliness, staging, supplies and cooling. Brandon relays Mom identifying cleaner acknowledgment/chasing as a major time burden, Tuesday trash as a coverage gap, and repair coordination/status uncertainty while away as especially overwhelming. Income and outside expenses are not consolidated, so profitability and pricing choices are unclear. An actual free eight-hour late checkout with extensive cooking reportedly required about two extra cleaning hours at unchanged cleaner pay. The earlier muddy-party scenario remains hypothetical. Same family/property reports; no invoices, independent observation or measured time study inspected. Follow-up 2026-09-09: Brandon explicitly says nobody currently could take responsibility if Mom were unavailable and cleaning coverage failed. This does not establish local provider scarcity. Clarification 2026-09-09: Mom has tried no other dedicated operations app besides the family-built app; earlier Airbnb/message use remains part of the workflow. The existing app is the comparison baseline. Follow-up E47: explicit cleaner acceptance/decline is not really present according to Brandon; wording qualified and implementation uninspected. E48: cleaner reportedly stopped using existing completion features because they were too difficult/annoying. Photo evidence informs payment, but the current workaround is unknown. Do not equate implemented completion features with continued use. E49-E52: Brandon explicitly offers a speculative interruption/navigation explanation; long room-by-room form and existing minimum-photo/grouping changes described. Cleaner in fifties with unspecified phone; age and near-universal smartphone adoption are not established causal/market evidence. Delegating substitute search remains a proposal. Follow-up E56-E62: actual app repository inspected at main/c2ba5cc. A13 is now the code baseline, superseding earlier implementation-unknown wording for the inspected paths only. Current compact cleaning UI, broader finance/AI modules and absence of a minimum-photo submit check may reflect later revisions. Deployed version, configuration and adoption remain unknown. Founder favors free-order capture and proposes assistive camera review/shared tablet; these are untested.
scope.ambition: User prefers an owner-facing automation/software business without a staffed cleaning service. Independent-provider referral/marketplace and professional-manager buyers remain exploratory alternatives. Exact income target, time budget and acceptable support burden unknown.
success_criteria: Proposed for next learning investment: identify a recurring, consequential problem in a reachable audience and a demonstrable gap versus the current alternative.
Commercial thresholds remain unknown: establish willingness to pay and continue, owner time savings, provider reliability, and support-adjusted economics before a larger commitment.

Candidate scoped outcome: fewer avoidable family reinspection visits while maintaining agreed readiness standards and acceptable provider effort; no numeric threshold or perfection guarantee established.

Proposed first mechanics test: two jobs accepted and accounted for by agreed cutoffs, no Mom confirmation-chasing and no unowned exception; total coordination and cleaner effort must be visible. Does not demonstrate market demand or reliability.
scope.next_investment: Prepare a bounded one-room reference/current image comparison after establishing reference-photo availability; use the existing app baseline and ordinary-camera capture first. No app build, hardware purchase or live cleaner trial committed.
constraints: Very simple experience and inexpensive price; exact fee unknown.
Two-programmer ambition and preference against operating a staffed cleaning service; local provider partnerships remain possible.
App setup/navigation and mandatory evidence steps burden substitute cleaners; reduce that burden while retaining adequate readiness assurance.
Exact city, supported hardware/integrations, provider supply, measured hours/cost and initial market remain unknown; rough recurrence estimates are now recorded.
Low-invasiveness preference; hardware is a possible tool only after identifying the specific condition that needs checking.
pending_questions: Does Mom already have photos of the rooms arranged exactly how she wants them?

hypotheses.current_assessment: No backup owner currently exists for the family. Software-plus-independent-provider arrangements remain possible, but the broader off-duty promise and support economics are untested.

hypotheses.claim: Supported-device monitoring and a defined recovery route reduce access/connection incidents requiring family intervention.
hypotheses.subject: C03

hypotheses.claim: The proposed Airbnb-guest email and discounted off-platform repeat-booking funnel is a viable distribution approach.

hypotheses.claim: Family post-cleaner inspections uncover actionable readiness gaps that the existing cleaner handover does not reliably address.
hypotheses.subject: C04

hypotheses.claim: An improved on-site work and handover process can reduce avoidable family reinspection while preserving agreed readiness standards at acceptable provider effort.
hypotheses.subject: C04

hypotheses.claim: A property-specific standards and feedback workflow reduces family effort when onboarding a cleaner and establishes a useful handover afterward.
hypotheses.subject: C04

hypotheses.claim: A clear exceptional-cleaning scope/time/price approval flow reduces coordination and compensates providers fairly when routine fixed-price work changes.
hypotheses.subject: C01
hypotheses.current_assessment: Now supported by an actual reported cooking/late-checkout extra-work incident as well as the earlier hypothetical. Fair workable approval rules and recurrence remain untested.

hypotheses.claim: Explicit cleaner acceptance, completion/exception reporting and an agreed backup owner reduce Mom's confirmation chasing without leaving work unowned.
hypotheses.subject: C01
hypotheses.current_assessment: Untested broader claim. No backup owner is available, and the existing completion workflow is reportedly not being used. Reliable acceptance/completion cannot be assumed from feature presence.

hypotheses.claim: A repair workflow with a responsible person, current status and explicit outcome/follow-up reporting reduces owner coordination and unresolved worry.
hypotheses.subject: C02
hypotheses.current_assessment: Untested proposed improvement grounded in family reports; existing alternatives and actual use remain to be compared.

hypotheses.claim: Consolidated income, property costs, exceptional spending and family effort in an understandable view help owners like Mom judge whether the rental is worthwhile and act on that information.
hypotheses.subject: C10
hypotheses.current_assessment: Consolidated ledger/reporting and bill-photo prefill exist in supplied checkout; deployment/use/data completeness unknown. A property-summary compensation classification inconsistency was reproduced with synthetic data. Financial clarity remains unestablished.

hypotheses.claim: Clear agreed checkout and exceptional-work rules, informed by property economics, reduce ad hoc decisions and unexpected cleaning work.
hypotheses.subject: C11
hypotheses.current_assessment: Untested proposed improvement grounded in family reports; existing alternatives and actual use remain to be compared.

hypotheses.claim: Proactive explicit confirmation of a specific cleaning window, visible to Mom, reduces her messages/calls solely to establish whether the cleaner will attend.
hypotheses.subject: C01
hypotheses.current_assessment: Current checklist status model is open/submitted; no dedicated acceptance/decline lifecycle found in inspected paths. Notification machinery exists but does not establish acknowledgment.

hypotheses.claim: A short final camera sequence with clear reference views and no repeated form navigation reduces cleaner interruption/reporting effort while retaining agreed readiness evidence.
hypotheses.subject: C04
hypotheses.current_assessment: Untested proposed variant; founder review is next, not evidence of actual cleaner usability, reduced total effort or adequate owner assurance.

hypotheses.claim: A job-specific free-capture photo inbox reduces cleaner navigation burden while keeping missing views, classification uncertainty and owner review effort manageable.
hypotheses.subject: C04
hypotheses.current_assessment: Founder-preferred variant. Static code confirms current item-associated uploads and reusable AI image plumbing, but no job-level capture/classification workflow. Usability and adequate evidence remain untested.

hypotheses.claim: Assistive comparison of current room images with owner-approved references catches useful visible staging deviations without excessive false alarms, missed issues or cleaner effort.
hypotheses.subject: C04
hypotheses.current_assessment: Untested implementation variant; no actual image comparison or cleaner-device trial. LiDAR is optional for H26 and does not certify readiness.

hypotheses.claim: A property-owned handheld capture device reduces setup and device variability enough to outweigh carrying, charging and sign-in burdens.
hypotheses.subject: C04
hypotheses.current_assessment: Untested implementation variant; no actual image comparison or cleaner-device trial. LiDAR is optional for H26 and does not certify readiness.

decisions.subject: Bounded inquiry into the actual contribution of the family post-cleaner readiness visit
decisions.intended_next_investment: Inspect one recent family readiness check to distinguish missing tasks, additional responsibilities and lack of confidence/evidence; then specify the smallest meaningful comparison.
decisions.rationale: The user described recurring reinspection and explicitly wants to avoid following the cleaner while preserving readiness. A recent visit can discriminate among missing work, extra work and reassurance without selecting technology.
contradictions: Regular checks may find nothing or cover tasks never assigned to cleaners.
Medium in-stay problems may consume more time despite occurring less frequently.
